title: The class of a correspondence
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], where $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k$ is its fixed algebraic closure. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in the fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$; put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $X,Y,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes. For such a scheme $T$, write $D(T,A)$ for the derived category of sheaves of $A$-modules on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ for its full bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Write $Z=Y\times_sX$ with projections $p_1:Z\to Y$ and $p_2:Z\to X$, and let $c:C\to Z$ be a $k$-morphism. Put $c_1=p_1c$ and $c_2=p_2c$, so that $c=(c_1,c_2)$ is the support morphism for a correspondence from $(X,K)$ to $(Y,L)$ [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs]. Use the derived pullback, tensor and internal Hom of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Assume that $c$ and $p_1$ are exceptionally admissible at $A$ [def-trf-admissibility], with their specified constructible exceptional adjoints and composition isomorphisms.

Then tensor–Hom adjunction, the projection
formula and exceptional adjunction give a canonical isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}\bigl(Rc_!A_C,
R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C,A)}\bigl(Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!L\bigr),
$$

natural in $K$ and $L$. For a correspondence
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!L$, its *class* $[u]$ is the inverse image of $u$
under this isomorphism; it is a class supported on $c$ with values in
$R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-supported-class], i.e. $[u]\in
H^0_C\bigl(Z,R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)\bigr)$.

proof.text: Write $M=Lp_2^*K$, $N=Rp_1^!L$, $B=Rc_!A_C$ and $E_M=Lc^*M$. The given $K,L$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}$. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], applied to the projection $p_2$ and then to $c$, $M$ and $E_M$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}$. The projection $p_2$ is the base change along $X\to s$ of the separated finite-type structure map $Y\to s$ of [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs], hence is separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. The admissibility hypothesis on $c$ includes that $c$ is separated of finite type. By the specified constructible adjoints in [def-trf-admissibility], $N$ is in $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ and $Rc^!N$ is in $D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$. The constant sheaf $A_C$ in degree zero is constructible: use the one-piece stratification, with constant finite stalk $A$, in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. It has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], since tensoring with the free rank-one module $A_C$ gives the original sheaf. Thus $B$ is also in $D^b_{ctf}$ by the functor $Rc_!$ in the admissibility datum. All exceptional adjunctions below are on these full constructible subcategories; no unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjoint is required.

Use the tensor-internal-Hom adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations], clause (i), and the tensor braiding of the geometric package [sk-d-six]. They give a bijection
$$T_{M,N}:\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M,N).$$
Explicitly $T_{M,N}(\phi)=\operatorname{uncurry}(\phi)\circ\beta_{B,M}$, where $\operatorname{uncurry}(\phi):M\otimes^{\mathrm L}B\to N$ is inverse to the adjunction bijection, and $\beta_{B,M}:B\otimes^{\mathrm L}M\to M\otimes^{\mathrm L}B$. The inverse sends $h$ to $\operatorname{curry}(h\circ\beta_{B,M}^{-1})$. This uses the ringed-site tensor-Hom adjunction at $(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A_Z)$; the Stacks references in the source field identify the normalization of the cited adjunction, rather than an additional uncited input.

source.place: Tag 08J8 (equation-internal-hom), Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); blueprint proof, first bijection

proof.text:
Apply [fix-prop-projection-formula] with $f=c$, first argument $A_C\in D^b_c(C,A)$ and second argument $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. It gives $\operatorname{PF}_M:B\otimes^{\mathrm L}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_!(A_C\otimes^{\mathrm L}E_M)$, natural in $M$. The unitor $\lambda_{E_M}:A_C\otimes^{\mathrm L}E_M\xrightarrow{\sim}E_M$ has inverse $e\mapsto1\otimes e$: the two composites are the identity by the balancing relation $a\otimes e=1\otimes ae$. These are chain maps because $A_C$ is in degree zero. They compute the derived unitor using [def-weil-derived-tensor], since the rank-one constant module is K-flat (its tensor functor is the identity, hence preserves acyclic complexes). Set
$$J_M=\operatorname{PF}_M^{-1}\circ Rc_!(\lambda_{E_M}^{-1}):Rc_!E_M\xrightarrow{\sim}B\otimes^{\mathrm L}M.$$
Precomposing by $J_M$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B\otimes^{\mathrm L}M,N)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(Rc_!E_M,N)$; its inverse precomposes by $J_M^{-1}$.

source.place: ## Proof, second bijection and tensor-unit identity

proof.text:
Let $\operatorname{adj}_c:\operatorname{Hom}_Z(Rc_!E_M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_C(E_M,Rc^!N)$ be the specified adjunction in [def-trf-admissibility]. If $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ denote its unit and counit, its maps are $h\mapsto Rc^!(h)\circ\eta_{E_M}$ and $v\mapsto\varepsilon_N\circ Rc_!(v)$; the triangle identities make them inverse. Consequently
$$\Psi_{M,N}(\phi)=\operatorname{adj}_c\bigl(T_{M,N}(\phi)\circ J_M\bigr)$$
is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_C(E_M,Rc^!N)$. Its inverse is the three inverse bijections of steps 2--4 in reverse order.

The coefficient identifications for constant sheaves in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] preserve every constant section $a\in A$. Their composite does the same, so under the canonical inverse-image composition comparison it is the coefficient identification for the composite: uniqueness of the constant-sheaf identification preserving constants proves compatibility. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to $h=c$, $k=p_2$ and these identified constant ring sheaves, and use $p_2c=c_2$ in [def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs]. This gives the natural isomorphism $a_K:Lc_2^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lc^*Lp_2^*K=E_M$. The composition isomorphisms specified with the exceptional-admissibility datum [def-trf-admissibility], for $c$ and $p_1$, give $b_L:Rc^!Rp_1^!L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_1^!L$, using $p_1c=c_1$. Thus the required bijection is
$$\Phi_{K,L}(\phi)=b_L\circ\Psi_{Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L}(\phi)\circ a_K.$$
Its inverse first sends $u$ to $b_L^{-1}\circ u\circ a_K^{-1}$ and then applies $\Psi^{-1}$. This proves bijectivity with exactly the stated endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); blueprint proof, last bijection and specified exceptional composition

proof.text:
Here is the naturality check before the endpoint identifications. For $m:M\to M'$, $n:N\to N'$ and $\phi:B\to R\mathcal Hom_A(M',N)$, write $H(m,n)$ for the internal-Hom map $R\mathcal Hom(M',N)\to R\mathcal Hom(M,N')$. The adjunction with parameter in [sk-def-sf-operations] and the natural braiding in [sk-d-six] give, by uncurry followed by braiding,
$$T_{M,N'}(H(m,n)\circ\phi)=n\circ T_{M',N}(\phi)\circ(1_B\otimes m).$$
Naturality of the projection formula [fix-prop-projection-formula] and of the unit maps $e\mapsto1\otimes e$ used in step 3 gives
$$(1_B\otimes m)\circ J_M=J_{M'}\circ Rc_!Lc^*(m).$$
Substitute this equality in the preceding formula and apply naturality of the adjunction [def-trf-admissibility] (equivalently insert $Rc^!(h)\eta$ from step 4 and use naturality of $\eta$). The result is
$$\Psi_{M,N'}(H(m,n)\circ\phi)=Rc^!(n)\circ\Psi_{M',N}(\phi)\circ Lc^*(m).$$
This checks both variables, including arbitrary derived morphisms, because the cited adjunctions and projection formula are natural transformations on the derived categories.

source.place: ## Proof, sentence asserting naturality of every arrow (expanded on morphisms)

proof.text:
For $f:K\to K'$, $g:L\to L'$ and $\phi:B\to R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K',Rp_1^!L)$, put $m=Lp_2^*(f)$ and $n=Rp_1^!(g)$ in step 6. The natural composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] says
$$Lc^*(m)\circ a_K=a_{K'}\circ Lc_2^*(f).$$
Naturality of the exceptional composition isomorphism included in [def-trf-admissibility] says
$$b_{L'}\circ Rc^!(n)=Rc_1^!(g)\circ b_L.$$
Multiplying the equality of step 6 on the left by $b_{L'}$ and on the right by $a_K$, and substituting these two equations, proves
$$\Phi_{K,L'}\bigl(R\mathcal Hom(Lp_2^*f,Rp_1^!g)\circ\phi\bigr)=Rc_1^!(g)\circ\Phi_{K',L}(\phi)\circ Lc_2^*(f).$$
Taking $f$ or $g$ to be the identity gives respectively naturality in $L$ and contravariant naturality in $K$.

source.place: ## Proof, naturality in K and L after composition identifications

proof.text: For the given coefficient morphism $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!L$, define $[u]=\Phi_{K,L}^{-1}(u)$. By construction $\Phi_{K,L}([u])=u$, and uniqueness follows from injectivity. By [def-trf-supported-class] with $i=c$, $T=C$ and $P=R\mathcal Hom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)$, its source set is exactly $H^0_C(Z,P)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}(Rc_!A_C,P)$. Thus this inverse image is the asserted supported class. The definition requires a specified separated finite-type map $c$, not an immersion; the given admissibility of $c$ supplies that domain.
